PartitionCompletenessArgument: Every supported guest term belongs to one listed runtime class; classification reads only the outer class, without traversing members or invoking functions. Arbitrary nesting or collection size cannot change the result.

Atoms include Boolean atoms, empty names and Unicode names; all are Atom. Integers use BigInteger with no small/bignum representation branch. Finite floating-point values, including both zero signs, subnormal and maximum finite, are FloatTerm.

Ordinary records are tuple terms; native records are a distinct term class and therefore false for is_tuple. Lists include Nil and Cons with proper or improper tail; aligned binaries and partial bitstrings remain BitString, false for these five predicates.
Local/external function identities, PIDs, references, resource references and ports remain nonpositive classes without identity resolution, liveness queries or side effects.
Entries.ErrorAndEffectContract: Exactly one admitted guest term always yields cached Boolean atom true/false. No guest error branch or observable side effect. Wrong arity is another MFA; expression failures occur before invocation. CLR null, arbitrary host-only Term subclasses and nonfinite FloatTerm values are outside the admitted guest term model.
